grid[gain.financial].definition: A holding that rises with the environment.
grid[gain.human].definition: The activity with the highest leverage on future earning — the profession being built, the qualification being taken, the venture being started.
grid[income.financial].definition: A holding that pays a steady distribution.
grid[income.human].definition: The dependable mandate or employment that pays the bills now.
grid[protection.financial].definition: A holding that pays in crisis — it pays exactly when nothing else does, and costs you something the rest of the time.
grid[protection.human].definition: What keeps a person functioning so the other three continue: health, network, the activity not done for money.
grid[stabilisation.financial].definition: A holding that peaks in contraction — it pays before the damage, not during it.
grid[stabilisation.human].definition: Smaller, unrelated earning streams that reduce the variance of the whole.

pensions[p1].ahv.levers[2].note: Erziehungsgutschriften, credited for years with children under 16 in the household.
pensions[p1].ahv.levers[3].note: Betreuungsgutschriften, for years spent caring for a relative.
pensions[p1].ahv.levers[4].note: Splitting, which halves and reassigns income earned during a marriage.
pensions[p1].ahv.levers[5].note: Jugendjahre, contribution years between 18 and 20 that can fill later gaps.
pensions[p1].ahv.levers[6].note: The revaluation factor applied to early-career income before the average is taken.
pensions[p1].ahv.levers[7].note: The reduction for drawing early and the supplement for deferring -- both in Merkblatt 3.04.
pensions[p1].bvg.levers[3].note: The überobligatorisch portion, which for most members is the larger one and is credited and converted at whatever the fund's regulations say.
pensions[p1].bvg.levers[4].note: Salary growth, and any change of pension fund.
pensions[p1].bvg.levers[5].note: Einkäufe — voluntary purchases into the fund, which are the single largest lever a member over 50 has.
pensions[p1].bvg.levers[6].note: A WEF withdrawal already taken, which reduces the balance and the future credits on it.
pensions[p1].bvg.levers[7].note: Risk and administration costs, which are charged alongside the credits and are not part of them.
pensions[p1].bvg.levers[8].note: A part-time pensum changing, which changes the coordinated salary more than proportionally.
pensions[p1].bvg.levers[9].note: Any fund that insures more than the obligatory minimum, which is nearly all of them.
